children: Apple
could enter the foldable smartphone market with an immediate supply problem, as early production of its long-rumored foldable iPhone is reportedly running at only a
few hundred units per day

. The constraint could create scarcity around one of Apple's most important new hardware categories in years, but it may also limit the product's near-term financial impact despite an expected price above $2,000.

The production bottleneck reportedly stems from Apple's unusually strict quality-control standards as manufacturing partners work to improve yields. Apple has not publicly confirmed the foldable iPhone.
TF International Securities analyst Ming-Chi Kuo previously estimated second-half 2026 assembly shipments of roughly
7 million to 8 million units
, including only
500,000 to 1 million units in the third quarter
. He expects pricing around
, positioning the device well above Apple's conventional Pro models.

That creates an unusual setup. Limited supply could reinforce the foldable iPhone's premium image and generate strong early demand, but Apple will need manufacturing yields to improve quickly if the device is to become a meaningful contributor to iPhone revenue.
By comparison, Kuo expects roughly
20 million to 22 million iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max shipments during Q3
, highlighting how small the foldable launch may initially be relative to Apple's core premium lineup.
The stakes are substantial because iPhone remains Apple's most important hardware business. Apple reported record June-quarter company revenue of
$109.4 billion, up 16% year over year
, with iPhone revenue also reaching a June-quarter record.
Investors Takeaway
Attention now turns to Apple's
September 9 product event
, which the company has officially scheduled for 10 a.m. Pacific time.
Investors should watch the foldable iPhone's
price, launch timing, availability and production guidance
. A device near $2,500 could materially lift average selling prices if Apple eventually scales production.

But prolonged supply constraints would cap unit volumes and delay that upside. The most important signal may therefore be how quickly Apple's manufacturing partners can move beyond the initial low-output phase without compromising the quality standards behind the bottleneck.

title: Apple's Foldable iPhone Runs Into Early Trouble
